title: Library of Alexandria
summary: A scalable, self-documenting library of knowledge — browse a tree of topics, highlight any term for an inline definition, and explore interactive lessons.

children.title: Spiking Neural Networks
children.summary: Neural networks whose neurons communicate via discrete spikes over time.

children.title: Neuron Models
children.summary: How individual spiking neurons integrate input and fire, from one-variable caricatures to full biophysics.

children.title: Leaky Integrate-and-Fire
children.summary: The workhorse: a leaky capacitor with a threshold and a reset.

children.title: Izhikevich Model
children.summary: Two variables, four parameters, twenty cortical firing patterns.

children.title: Exponential Integrate-and-Fire
children.summary: LIF with a smooth exponential spike-initiation zone instead of a hard threshold.

children.title: Adaptive Exponential Integrate-and-Fire
children.summary: EIF plus a slow adaptation current: adaptation, bursting and more.

children.title: Hodgkin-Huxley Model
children.summary: The biophysical benchmark: spikes from sodium and potassium channel kinetics.

children.title: FitzHugh-Nagumo Model
children.summary: A two-variable caricature of Hodgkin-Huxley for phase-plane thinking.

children.title: Morris-Lecar Model
children.summary: A two-variable conductance model with calcium and potassium currents.

children.title: Spike Response Model
children.summary: Voltage as a sum of kernels triggered by input and by the neuron's own spikes.

children.title: Stochastic Integrate-and-Fire
children.summary: Integrate-and-fire with noise: variability, escape rates and probabilistic spiking.

children.title: Multi-Compartment Model
children.summary: Neurons as trees of coupled compartments, so dendrites can compute.

children.title: Spike Encoding
children.summary: Turning real-valued signals into spike trains: rate, latency and population codes.

children.title: Neuron Filters
children.summary: Synaptic and membrane filters that shape how spike trains are integrated in time.

children.title: Learning Rules
children.summary: How synapses change: STDP and its variants, three-factor rules, BCM and surrogate gradients.

children.title: Classical Additive STDP
children.summary: Pre-before-post strengthens, post-before-pre weakens, decaying with the gap.

children.title: Triplet STDP
children.summary: Spike triplets and slow traces reproduce frequency effects pair rules miss.

children.title: Anti-STDP
children.summary: The flipped window: causal pairings weaken, cancelling predictable input.

children.title: Symmetric STDP
children.summary: Potentiation for near-coincidence in either order: a synchrony detector.

children.title: Multiplicative STDP
children.summary: Weight-dependent updates that keep weights bounded and unimodal.

children.title: Voltage-Dependent STDP
children.summary: Plasticity gated by postsynaptic voltage, after Clopath and colleagues.

children.title: Reward-Modulated STDP
children.summary: Eligibility traces plus a global reward signal: a three-factor rule.

children.title: BCM Rule
children.summary: A rate rule with a sliding threshold that keeps activity in range.

children.title: Surrogate Gradient
children.summary: Training spiking networks by backpropagation with a smooth stand-in for the spike's derivative.

children.title: Neuroscience
children.summary: The biology the models aim at: cortical columns, population dynamics, insect brains and neural manifolds.

children.title: Cortical Columns
children.summary: The neocortex's repeating circuit and the computational theories built on it.

children.title: The Thousand Brains Theory
children.summary: Every column learns whole objects in its own reference frame; columns vote to agree.

children.title: Temporal Memory and Minicolumns
children.summary: How cells in minicolumns learn sequences and predictions with dendritic segments.

children.title: Grid Cells and Reference Frames
children.summary: Location codes from grid-cell modules, and why columns need them.

children.title: Building a Column from Spiking Neurons
children.summary: A practical plan for a spiking cortical column: layers, circuits, learning rules and experiments.

children.title: Neuronal Dynamics
children.summary: Phase planes, bifurcations and population activity: the mathematics of how neurons behave.

children.title: Mushroom Bodies
children.summary: The insect learning center: sparse expansion, pattern separation and valence readout.

children.title: Neural Manifolds
children.summary: Low-dimensional structure in population activity, attractors and synchronization.

children.title: Foundations
children.summary: Frameworks for building cognition from spiking neurons: the NEF, semantic pointers and Legendre memory.

children.title: Neural Engineering Framework
children.summary: Representation, transformation and dynamics: compiling math into spiking networks.

children.title: Semantic Pointers
children.summary: High-dimensional vectors bound and bundled into structured symbols.

children.title: Legendre Memory Unit
children.summary: An optimal continuous-time memory built on the Legendre delay network.

children.title: Neuromorphic Hardware
children.summary: Chips that compute the way spiking networks do: event-driven, parallel, memory beside compute.

children.title: Loihi
children.summary: Intel's research chips with programmable on-chip learning.

children.title: TrueNorth
children.summary: IBM's million-neuron, low-power, fixed-synapse chip.

children.title: SpiNNaker
children.summary: Manchester's many-ARM-core machine for real-time spiking simulation.

children.title: FPGA Neuromorphic Systems
children.summary: Building spiking networks on reconfigurable logic.

children.title: Calculus
children.summary: A template topic: the mathematics of continuous change, from limits and derivatives to integrals.

children.title: Limits
children.summary: The foundational idea of approaching a value, underpinning both derivatives and integrals.

children.title: Derivatives
children.summary: Instantaneous rates of change and the slope of a curve at a point.

children.title: Integrals
children.summary: Accumulation and area under a curve — the inverse of differentiation.

children.title: Game Theory
children.summary: A template topic: the study of strategic decision-making among rational agents.

children.title: Nash Equilibrium
children.summary: A strategy profile where no player can gain by unilaterally changing their own strategy.

children.title: Dominant Strategies
children.summary: Strategies that yield a better outcome for a player regardless of what the others do.

children.title: Prisoner's Dilemma
children.summary: The classic game showing why two rational agents may fail to cooperate even when it serves them both.
